In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of RSG facilitates successful removal of metastatic lesions, despite negative conventional imaging, if scintigraphically positive.
RGS is not only a safe but also a very efficient tool for the detection of neuroendocrine tumor lesions.
123I-MIB-G scintigraphy and RGS are useful in patients with neuroendocrine tumors and should be considered in patients who are candidates for surgery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined use of octreotide- and MIBG-scan is superior to either of them alone in the localization of neuroendocrine tumors.
123I-MIBg scintigraphy is a useful tool for the localization of neuroendocrine lesions and may be superior to octreoscan in certain situations.
123I-MIBGs scintigraphy is superior to111In-pentreotide in the detection of carcinoid metastases, if the involved sites are located in the proximity to the highly octreotide avid organs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RGS using123I-MBGS may be useful for the detection of neuroendocrine tumor metastases in patients with negative conventional imaging.
the combined use of RGS and123I-MABG scintigraphy is a promising tool for the detection and resection even of small neuroendocrine tumors and their metastases.
